newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's cabinet to meet before confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy's cabinet to meet before confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's cabinet will meet on Thursday at 1245 GMT, hours before the centre-left government faces a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said late on Wednesday that the government would meet to confirm its request for the confidence vote, which is scheduled for 1700 GMT.
Opposition parties were particularly angered that the government had called a vote to ram through a long-stalled draft law on civil service reforms.

The cabinet agenda also includes a decree on Italy's involvement in Albania, where it is leading a multinational security force, and a decree to implement European Union legislation on transborder capital movement.
A draft law to ratify accords between Italy and Russia on cooperating in exchange controls and fighting money laundering will also be discussed, Prodi's office said in a statement.

The law on civil service reforms, passed by the Senate (upper house) last July, has been stalled in the lower Chamber of Deputies by opposition politicians absenting themselves repeatedly, ensuring a quorum was not achieved.
The confidence test is designed to approve with a simple yes or no vote those articles of the draft legislation that have yet to be passed. If the government loses, it falls.

Prodi has no majority in the Chamber of Deputies, where he relies on the support of hard-left Communist Refoundation allies who have proved difficult partners since the government took office a year ago.
Refoundation caused waves last week when they voted against the deployment of a security force for Albania. The force was approved with votes from the centre-right opposition.
The hard-left party later fell back into line by backing the government in two confidence votes in parliament, necessary to reconfirm the majority behind Prodi.
